sam_support: Customer reported embeddings throughput collapse last night. vectors/sec dropped ~80% while tokens/sec stayed ~constant. No auth failures reported. Raising here for triage — @maya_eng @chris_infra :eyes:

customer_prod: We started seeing 429s around 02:12 UTC, model=embed-redwood-1536, batch_size=8 in client, payloads unchanged. Sample request id: abc123-def456. Later a few requests returned 400 Dimension mismatch.

sam_support: Can you paste a minimal failing payload and the error body? Also what region / pool are you hitting?

customer_prod: hitting eu-west-1 / embeddings-prod. Example failing curl below (we only redact api_key):

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \\  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\  -d '{"model":"embed-redwood-1536","input":["foo","bar","baz","qux","quux","corge","grault","garply"]}'
```

response (snippet):

```json
{"error":{"message":"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768 for item 3","type":"invalid_request_error","code":400}}
```

sam_support: Hmm — dimension mismatch + 429s + tokens stable suggests routing/variant issue rather than upstream tokenizer change. Attaching runtime logs we pulled: (shortened)

```
[02:14:22] embeddings-prod: kv_cache_queue_depth=238 pending_batches=46 avg_batch_size=2.1 gpu_util=97%
[02:15:03] embeddings-prod: rate_limit_throttle=429 spikes=320 per_min
[02:15:40] variant-router: route embed-redwood-1536 -> embed-redwood-1536-v2-quant at 01:55 by rollout/auto-split
```

maya_eng: We rolled a conservative autosplit last night to test the quantized variant (v2-quant) for cost savings. It looks like v2-quant was accidentally receiving more traffic and it expects 768-dim embeddings (we onboarded a trimmed model) — that explains the 400s. The throughput regression is explained by smaller effective batch packing on v2 which increases GPU inefficiency (avg_batch_size dropped).

chris_infra: Confirming: routing change was triggered by rollout service at 01:55 UTC and hit 25% for a short window; we reverted the split at 02:40. After revert we see vectors/sec climb back toward baseline and queue depth fall.

ops_bot: deploy-bot: rollout/auto-split changed traffic for embed-redwood-1536 -> 25% embed-redwood-1536-v2-quant at 2026-01-18T01:55:12Z by maya_eng

erica_research: Repro steps to validate locally: send 1k single-item requests at qps=20 to the variant endpoint and compare vectors/sec vs tokens/sec. Suggested script:

```bash
# send 1000 single-input requests at 20 qps
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \\  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDDIT_KEY" \\  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\  -d '{"model":"embed-redwood-1536","input":"test-'$i'"}' &
  sleep 0.05
done
```

And monitor runtime metrics: `rbctl metrics get gpu_queue_depth --pool embeddings-prod --window 5m` and `rbctl traces query --filter "route:embed-redwood-1536-v2-quant" --limit 50`.

maya_eng: Immediate mitigation we applied: full rollback of autosplit (done at 02:40), pinned customer to stable variant for now, added dimension-checking in edge-proxy to return clearer 400 before hitting GPU.

chris_infra: Longer term ops items: (1) add pre-routing validation for expected embedding dim per model variant, (2) telemetry alert if avg_batch_size drops >50% from baseline, (3) autosplit throttle cap for quantized variants so we don't overwhelm smaller instances.

sam_support: Customer-facing follow-up: created support ticket SUP-7421, notified customer, included repro instructions and timeline. Customer asked about billing for 429s — finance/sales, please advise on credits.

customer_prod: Thanks — appreciate quick rollback. We'll run repro tests and report back. Can you also share the exact subset of requests that hit v2-quant (request ids) so we can correlate client logs?

maya_eng: Will dump request ids from router logs and upload to the ticket (redacted). Also adding a one-off regression test to catch quantized-serving perf drop in future canaries. :+1:

sam_support: Action items summary: 1) rollback (done), 2) upload router request ids (maya), 3) add pre-validation + alerting (eng/infra), 4) discuss billing credits (support & finance). Leaving thread open until SUP-7421 closed. :white_check_mark:
